overview.tagline: The whole story; for the formation of the church.
overview.purpose: Scripture does not merely inform the church—it forms it. OBS Theological Formation walks communities through fifty biblical narratives so they observe, discuss, apply, serve, and share each story in their heart language.
overview.obs: Open Bible Stories recounts fifty key narratives from Creation to New Creation. Together they are one unified account of what God has done, is doing, and will do—designed to form the community that tells them, not isolated lessons.
overview.fiveMovements: Each story uses a fivefold process (Biblical Interpretation → Theological Dialogue → Personal Reflection → Ministry Practice → Missional Outreach), framed by Community Study before and Conclusion after. Every movement is meant not just to inform but to form.

movements.name: Biblical Interpretation
movements.purpose: Observing the details of the story
movements.description: Exegetical movement: grasp what the text says. Observe story details and clarify translation terms before discussing meaning.

movements.name: Theological Dialogue
movements.purpose: Discussing the meaning of the story
movements.description: Theological movement: discuss what the text means. Discourse and theological questions, then draft each story panel and record translation decisions.

activities.name: Translation Draft
activities.purpose: Draft each story panel and record translation decisions

movements.name: Personal Reflection
movements.purpose: Following the teaching of the story
movements.description: Personal movement: apply what the text commands. Journal reflection, then team quality checking for accuracy, clarity, and naturalness.

activities.name: Team Check
activities.purpose: Check draft for accuracy, clarity, naturalness, consistency

movements.name: Ministry Practice
movements.purpose: Serving the church with the story
movements.description: Ecclesial movement: minister the text in the church community—plan how this story serves the local church.

movements.name: Missional Outreach
movements.purpose: Sharing the truth of the story (evangelism)
movements.description: Missional movement: announce the text to the surrounding world—plan witness and outreach beyond the church.

before.name: Community Study
before.purpose: Community formation activity / devotion before the five movements

after.name: Conclusion
after.purpose: Community review reflection and handoff of revised draft

formationPlan.summary: Optional dialogues before or alongside OBS so the community engages stories with a shared focus on mission, church, and Christian formation.

dialogues.name: Mission: Participating in God’s Purpose Together
dialogues.keyQuestion: What is the mission of your network? Who has God called you to reach?

dialogues.name: Church: Keeping God’s Church in the Center
dialogues.keyQuestion: What is the makeup and structure of your church network? Who are the key leaders?

dialogues.name: Formation: Engaging God’s Word for Transformation
dialogues.keyQuestion: How are Christians and churches in your context maturing in the faith?

dialogues.name: Summary of Formation Plan
dialogues.keyQuestion: How will your church or network approach theological formation?

source.title: OBS + Theological Formation
